title: Trade exposure and social cohesion: evidence from Uganda
summary: Does trade exposure change social cohesion? Using Uganda's exchange rate liberalisation as a natural experiment, the paper finds significant, though economically small, effects on trust, participation and identity.
keyFindings: Exposure to exchange rate shocks reduces trust and enhances participation, with ambiguous effects on identity.
The effects run mainly through the expenditure channel (household exposure), and to a lesser extent through earnings (worker and firm exposure).
methods: Micro tax data and a natural experiment (Uganda's exchange rate liberalisation), with firm, worker and household exposure measures.
